key_insight: A message-passing reinforcement learning policy coordinates global and node-level control on dynamic networks while respecting permutation symmetries and transparency constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports network-wide resource decisions coupled with local allocations, such as distributing capital interventions across interconnected financial institutions.
method: Use a message-passing neural network with separate global and local policy heads.
Derive explicit Lipschitz bounds for input and parameter perturbations.
Use these bounds to establish projected policy-gradient convergence guarantees.
evidence_signal: Numerical systemic-risk experiments report better performance than feedforward-network baselines and scaling to large networks, but the abstract provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Sensitivity and optimization guarantees depend on architectural choices and graph characteristics, so robustness should be checked for the target network.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
